exposure: Neonatal microbial colonization (simple association with starter microbiota vs. complex association with sow's diluted feces)
Jejunal perfusion with enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli F4 (ETEC)
Jejunal perfusion with purified F4 fimbriae
outcome: Jejunal gene expression (Affymetrix Porcine Gene 1.1_ST array)
Up-regulation and down-regulation of gene sets
Networks related to inflammatory and immune responses
cohort: The study included 12 caesarian-derived pigs, neonatally associated with microbiota of different complexity.
finding: The study found that the nature of neonatal microbial colonization significantly impacts the jejunal molecular response to microbial stimuli later in life, with complex microbiota leading to modulated immune and inflammatory responses.
